newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 492.00/493.00/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 492.00/493.00/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed weaker at 492.00/493.00 per dollar Wednesday as interest rates dropped and the Central Bank did not respond to heavy currency demand, traders said.
Yields on the benchmark six month TEM bills fell by 88 basis points to 19.54 percent, bringing their drop nearly four percentage points in the last month.
The drop in interest yields spurred on already strong dollar demand, traders said.
"The Central Bank intervened very little, it only met corporate demand," one trader said.
Traders said the bolivar could continue to slip if the Central Bank did not respond to the high currency demand in coming days.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
Venezuela continues to pursue an inflation-fighting strong bolivar policy, where the currency ostensibly floats between slowly depreciating bands set by Central Bank intervention.
Critics say the policy has left the bolivar increasingly over-valued with the exchange rate little-changed since price and currency controls were removed in April last year.
